scope_notes: Pearl Definition 1 (d-separation, p. 106) and its illustrations (path blocking on the chain, Berkson's paradox, the two-coin example, the remark that d-separation implications are the main opening for testing, note 7) were treated as the extent of the graphical-separation chapter, which cites Definition 1 p. 106, and were not counted against these components. The sec. 3 introduction above sec. 3.1 on p. 103 was treated as outside the cited sections.

Lauritzen p. 68: only its opening remark (a structural-equation network need not have a density with respect to any product measure; covered by thm:p16-measurable-graph-examples and body 10-12) was counted; (F), Proposition 2.51, Lemma 2.52 and Theorem 2.53 are not among the locator's named results.

The p. 65 lead-in contrast with the undirected case is preserved in substance (only S1-S4; no intersection, positivity or probability: body 209-211).
Lauritzen Theorem 1.28 is preserved in kernel form for every parameter; the joint-law transfer for an independent uniform is written in the whole-model paragraph (annex 276-312).

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C002 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-ci-calculus, but the full proof is missing for the clause 'Measurable functions may be applied to either independent tuple, also using the conditioning tuple as an argument' (body measurable-causal-graphs.tex 47-48). Its only argument is a one-clause sketch at annex 53-56: 'by pushing forward the conditional product kernels at each z'. Nothing shows that the regular conditional law of (g(X,Z),h(Y,Z)) given Z=z is the image of the conditional product law at z. The substitution identity of thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure that would give this is neither used nor cited, and the proof never returns from that identity to the product-test definition. The Z-free case, both equivalences and the four semigraphoid properties are fully argued.
duties.note: Annex 63-102 builds the image kernel rho from the conditional kernel pi of (X,Y) given Z and identifies it as the regular conditional law of (g(X,Z),h(Y,Z)) via the final sentence of thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure (the substitution identity); 104-119 shows it is the image of the product off one null set N; 121-143 returns to the product-test definition by Fubini.

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C005 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-kernel-randomization, but the full proof is missing for the 'Consequently' assertion (body 90-94): every finite standard Borel kernel model has a representation X_v=F_v(X_pa(v),U_v) with mutually independent uniform U_v. Annex 157-160 says only 'Topological evaluation and successive conditioning show that its joint law is the kernel law'. It does not show that U_v is independent of the predecessors already constructed, that K_v(X_pa(v),.) is therefore their conditional law, or that induction identifies the joint law with P_K. The matching argument later at annex 508-513 is not invoked. The single-kernel realization (112-155) and the non-uniqueness example (160-166) are complete.
duties.note: Annex 259-312: induction proving U_{v_k} independent of X_{P_{k-1}}, K_{v_k}(X_pa,.) a regular conditional law given all predecessors (Tonelli on the product law), and mu_k = P_K^(k) by rectangle uniqueness; order independence via the construction theorem.

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C010 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-response-component, but the full proof is missing for the stated consequence (body 304-307): one conditional product law of (R,B) given C licenses integration of the whole family at a measurable random parameter depending on (B,C). Annex 567-573 is a two-sentence sketch. It does not derive L(R|B,C)=L(R|C) as kernels from R independent of B given C, and it does not substitute the random parameter into F via thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure. Separately, annex 537-538 ('by the separation hypothesis') relies, without stating or citing them, on two facts: exposing private roots preserves d-separation (stated only later, at 580-581) and the moral-separation bridge. The pointwise representation and R independent of B given C are argued (545-565).
duties.note: Root exposure is now a lemma stated (body 304-316) and proved (annex 834-860) before use and cited with thm:p16-moral-separation-bridge at annex 870-874; annex 929-944 derives L(R|B,C)=L(R|C) as kernels from the first equivalence; 949-976 substitutes theta(B,C) into F via thm:p15-kernel-joint-measure and tower; 978-991 signed case and null sets.

duties.duty: ED26-P16-CH-measurable-causal-graphs-C012 (partial): The status is proved=annex:p16.measurable-mediation-fields, but the proof of item 1 (body 364-365) is incomplete. In the cross-world field, annex 610-611 claims 'The mediator tuple in this auxiliary model is exactly M_b, by topological evaluation on its restored ancestors'. For that, every exposure child that is an ancestor of a mediator must lie outside D_Y; annex 607-608 gives exposure input a to every exposure child in D_Y. The listed 'exact graph facts' (594-605) put into D_M only the heads of restored edges and their parents. No step places the other exposure children among the mediator ancestors in D_M, so the construction of M_b, and with it R_0 independent of M_b given C, is not fully argued. The claim at 613-615 that every vertex needed for Y belongs to D_Y is likewise only asserted. Items 2 and 3 and the reference-mediator law are argued.
duties.note: Fact 1 (annex 1026-1039) places every exposure descendant that is a mediator ancestor in D_M; Fact 5 (1111-1126) proves the auxiliary mediator tuple is M_b with input b at every such vertex; Fact 6 (1128-1148) proves the auxiliary response is Y_{a,m} and that every vertex needed for Y lies in D_Y; Facts 2-4 supply the ancestral set, separation and unchanged C.
